ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy New Potato → Spanish Jam suite with soaring Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The February ’68 Carousel Ballroom set delivers a monster New Potato Caboose into Spanish Jam and an all‑out Alligator‑Caution‑Feedback run. Pigpen’s organ shines on The Other One and Cryptical Envelopment, while Jerry’s guitar soars through the Dark Star > China Cat Sunflower > The Eleven sequence. A complete soundboard capture makes this a must‑listen for any Deadhead.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at the Carousel Ballroom on February 14, 1968 is pure psychedelic fire. The first set rolls from a heartfelt Morning Dew into a seamless Dark Star → China Cat Sunflower → The Eleven suite that showcases Jerry’s soaring leads and Phil’s manic bass improvisations, capped off by an exuberant Turn On Your Lovelight. The second set is the real beast: Cryptical Envelopment segues into The Other One before diving into a legendary New Potato Caboose → Spanish Jam flow, then launches into an unbroken Alligator → Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback marathon that still feels fresh today. Pigpen’s calliope organ dominates the early jams, adding depth to The Other One and The Eleven, while Mickey and Bill lock in a tight, symbiotic eight‑limb rhythm foundation. The encore’s In The Midnight Hour rounds out a high‑energy night that remains one of the most celebrated shows of ’68.

best_recording.reason: Excellent two‑track soundboard capture of the full concert with crisp clarity and only a brief splice in the Alligator jam, providing the most complete listening experience.

key_highlights: Monster New Potato Caboose → Spanish Jam sequence that defines the second set.
Alligator → Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback suite runs uninterrupted.
Dark Star > China Cat Sunflower > The Eleven showcases soaring guitar and inventive bass lines.
Pigpen’s organ dominates The Other One and Cryptical Envelopment, adding psychedelic depth.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers a crisp, crunchy tone with soaring solos; his lead work drives the Dark Star suite and fuels the Alligator‑Caution jam.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s manic bass lines provide both propulsion and melodic counterpoint, especially during New Potato Caboose and the extended improvisations after vocals.
band_performance.Bob: Weir anchors the rhythm with solid guitar chops and contributes strong vocal presence on Turn On Your Lovelight.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s rhythmic textures weave seamlessly with Bill, forming a symbiotic eight‑limb machine that locks down every jam.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann adds tight, propulsive drumming, complementing Hart and driving the high‑energy flow throughout both sets.
